prompt:
You are a Senior Financial Analyst on Chevron Corp's (CVX) Corporate FP&A team. The Controller has asked you to prepare a quarterly variance analysis comparing Q1 2026 operating performance against Q3 2025, the most recent comparable quarterly period. This analysis will be presented at the upcoming earnings review meeting with the CFO and will feed into the mid-year budget discussion.

Materials provided:
- Chevron Corp (CVX) Q1 2026 XBRL financial data including Revenues ($48.6B), RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax ($47.6B), CostOfGoodsAndServicesSold ($28.3B), SellingGeneralAndAdministrativeExpense ($1.1B), NetIncomeLoss ($2.2B), and EarningsPerShareDiluted ($1.11)
- Chevron Corp (CVX) Q3 2025 XBRL financial data including the same metrics: Revenues ($49.7B), RevenueExclTax ($48.2B), COGS ($27.4B), SG&A ($1.5B), Net Income ($3.5B), EPS ($1.82)
- Chevron Corp (CVX) FY 2025 full-year figures for the same metrics as a reference benchmark: Revenues ($189.0B), RevenueExclTax ($184.4B), COGS ($108.2B), SG&A ($5.1B), Net Income ($12.3B), EPS ($6.63)
- Recent filing history showing 10-Q filed 2026-05-07

Task requirements:
1. Build an Excel workbook with three tabs: 'Inputs', 'Variance Analysis', and 'Summary'.
2. The 'Inputs' tab must house all raw quarterly figures from Q1 2026 and Q3 2025 for: Revenues, RevenueExclAssessedTax, COGS, SG&A, Net Income, and EPS (Diluted). Also include the FY 2025 annual figures for these same metrics as a reference column. All dollar figures must be stated in millions (divide raw XBRL values by 1,000,000). EPS remains as-is.
3. The 'Variance Analysis' tab must calculate for each metric: (a) Q1 2026 value, (b) Q3 2025 value, (c) absolute variance (Q1 2026 minus Q3 2025), (d) percentage variance as (Q1 2026 - Q3 2025) / Q3 2025 formatted as a percentage, and (e) Q1 2026 as a percentage of FY 2025 annual total. All formulas must cell-reference the Inputs tab.
4. The 'Summary' tab must contain written commentary addressing: (a) the two largest positive variances and two largest negative variances by absolute dollar magnitude, (b) an assessment of whether Q1 2026 gross margin (defined as (Revenues - COGS) / Revenues) and net margin (Net Income / Revenues) improved or deteriorated versus Q3 2025, and (c) a brief note on how Q1 2026 net income compares to the quarterly run-rate implied by dividing FY 2025 annual net income by 4.
5. Display dollar amounts with comma separators and one decimal place. Percentage variances formatted as percentages with one decimal place. EPS with two decimal places.
6. The Inputs tab is the single source of truth. All calculations on the Variance Analysis tab must reference Inputs via cell references, not hardcoded numbers.

cells.value: Chevron Corp (CVX) - Q1 2026 vs Q3 2025 Variance Analysis Summary
Largest Variances by Absolute Dollar Amount

Largest Negative Variance #1: Net Income declined by $1,329.0M from Q3 2025 ($3,539.0M) to Q1 2026 ($2,210.0M), a -37.6% decrease. This is the largest unfavorable variance by absolute dollar magnitude.
Largest Negative Variance #2: COGS increased by $867.0M from Q3 2025 ($27,398.0M) to Q1 2026 ($28,265.0M), representing a +3.2% increase.
Largest Positive Variance #1: SG&A decreased by $458.0M from Q3 2025 ($1,524.0M) to Q1 2026 ($1,066.0M), a -30.1% reduction. This is the largest favorable variance by absolute dollar magnitude.
Largest Positive Variance #2: Revenues declined by only $1,119.0M (Q3 2025: $49,726.0M vs Q1 2026: $48,607.0M), a -2.2% decrease, relatively contained versus the net income decline.

Gross Margin: Q1 2026 = (48,607.0 - 28,265.0) / 48,607.0 = 41.8%. Q3 2025 = (49,726.0 - 27,398.0) / 49,726.0 = 44.9%. Gross margin deteriorated by approximately 3.1 percentage points quarter-over-quarter.
Net Margin: Q1 2026 = 2,210.0 / 48,607.0 = 4.5%. Q3 2025 = 3,539.0 / 49,726.0 = 7.1%. Net margin deteriorated by approximately 2.6 percentage points.

FY 2025 annual net income of $12,299.0M implies a quarterly run-rate of $3,074.8M ($12,299.0 / 4). Q1 2026 net income of $2,210.0M is $864.8M below this implied quarterly run-rate, representing a 28.1% shortfall. Q1 2026 is tracking well below FY 2025's annual pace.
Source: Chevron Corp XBRL filings. 10-Q filed 2026-05-07.
